articles.headline: Maxey, Sixers turn Philly boos into cheers in 29-point comeback over Cavaliers
articles.description: Booed after trailing by 24 at the half, the Sixers rode a game-high 32 points from Tyrese Maxey to erase a 29-point deficit and stun the Cavs 114-106 on Thursday.
articles.headlineJa: マクシーとシクサーズ、29点差をひっくり返す逆転劇でフィラデルフィアのブーイングを歓声に変え、キャバリアーズに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 前半に24点差をつけられブーイングを浴びたシクサーズだったが、タイリース・マクシーがゲームハイの32得点を挙げ、29点差を跳ね返して木曜日の試合を114-106で制し、キャバリアーズを stunning（驚愕）させた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The crowd at Xfinity Arena watched the Sixers cut a 29-point deficit to 10 in the third quarter Thursday night when Tyrese Maxey caught a pass from LeBron James in transition and, without taking a dribble, launched a 3-pointer.

As the ball went through the net, forcing the Cavs to call a timeout, Maxey walked toward the fans behind the scorers' table and screamed as Jaylen Brown flanked him in celebration and Joel Embiid celebrated on the other end of the court.

On a team laden with stars, it was Maxey who was the conductor of this raucous Philadelphia crowd, which followed his lead all night as the Sixers roared back to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106.

The 29-point comeback was the Cavaliers' largest blown lead and the Sixers' largest comeback in the play-by-play era. It was also the largest comeback of James' now 24-year career.

"It was just a great moment," said Maxey, who led all scorers with 32 points and six assists. "The crowd was into the game. We were just feeding off the crowd, feeding off our energy, feeding off our resilience."

Two nights after their season-opening win over the reigning champion New York Knicks, the Sixers were outclassed in nearly every way to begin Thursday night's game. They turned the ball over, couldn't get stops and missed layups.

Brown had just four points in his lowest-scoring first half at home since March 2025, while the Sixers' 15 first-half turnovers were their most in a half since January 2024. The Cavs' 69-45 halftime lead tied their largest in a season-opening half in franchise history and matched their largest halftime lead over the 76ers in franchise history.

As the first half came to a close, the Xfinity Arena crowd, most wearing the white opening night shirts with the Sixers roster and coach Nick Nurse printed on them, loudly booed.

Maxey said he challenged the group during the intermission.

"I said, well, it's time to see what we made of. Are we going to be some front-runners and only be happy when stuff is good?" Maxey said. "Or when stuff is bad, are we going to fight and be resilient? And we did that."

The Sixers responded with a quarter that Brown said "shifted the game," coming out of the break on an 8-0 run and outscoring Cleveland 37-21 in the third quarter.

Still, the Sixers went into the fourth trailing by eight. It wasn't until the 6:54 minute mark that they took the lead, when Embiid hit a 16-foot jump shot over center Jarrett Allen that gave Philadelphia its first lead, one it wouldn't relinquish.

Embiid said the team's resilience Thursday night was different from past teams he has been a part of during his 11-year Sixers career.

"No shade to anybody that's been here, but in the past, a lot of people would've just laid down and tried to move on to the next one," Embiid said.

He added: "Yeah, it was different. I said last game, after the game, it just feels different."

articles.headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's record 20-point streak ends in Thunder win over Nuggets
articles.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's historic streak of 20-point games ended Thursday night when he finished with 17 in a 96-84 win over the Nuggets.
articles.headlineJa: シャイ・ギルジャス＝アレクサンダーの20得点連続記録がストップ、サンダーはナゲッツに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜夜のナゲッツ戦で、サンダーは96-84で勝利したが、シャイ・ギルジャス＝アレクサンダーは17得点に終わり、歴史的な20得点連続記録が途絶えた。
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had his first game with fewer than 20 points in nearly two years, finishing with 17 points in Thursday night's 96-84 home win over the Denver Nuggets to snap his NBA-record streak of 20-point games.

Gilgeous-Alexander, who scored 32 points in a convincing win over San Antonio on Tuesday night, shot just 6 of 19 from the field against Denver in failing to reach 20 points for the first time since Oct. 30, 2024, a streak of 141 regular-season games.

He had just under two minutes left to score three more points and extend his streak, but with Oklahoma City up 93-76 with 1:43 left, he asked Thunder coach Mark Daigneault to sub him out.

"I was going to go out there, and then I saw that [the Nuggets] had subbed, so I thought we should sub, too," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "You always treat the game with respect."

Daigneault said he wanted to leave Gilgeous-Alexander in the game because a "historic streak" was on the line and praised his star player's maturity.

"I just think of the class that it shows and the perspective that it shows for him to say, 'Hey, I'm out now. The game's calling for me to be subbed out,'" Daigneault said. "That was his substitution. And of all the things that I admire about him, that's toward the top of the list in terms of moments that I appreciate about him."

Gilgeous-Alexander, the league's two-time reigning MVP, missed all seven shots he took in the first 24 minutes Thursday night as the Thunder trailed by as many as nine points. A pair of free throws kept him from going scoreless in a half for the first time since his rookie season with the Clippers in 2019.

It marked just the fourth time in 450 games with the Thunder that he has gone without a field goal in a half. Gilgeous-Alexander scored the first basket of the third quarter to pull Oklahoma City to 48-46.

Aaron Gordon scored 20 points, and Nikola Jokic and DeMar DeRozan added 13 apiece for Denver, which was playing its first game.

A layup by Mitchell gave the Thunder a 64-62 lead -- their first since 3-0 -- and 3-pointers by Alex Caruso and Gilgeous-Alexander extended it to 70-64 after three quarters. Oklahoma City pushed the advantage to 93-76 on a 3 by Gilgeous-Alexander to give him 17 points with 1:44 left. He then asked to be taken out during a timeout and did not return to the game.

Jalen Williams scored 21 points, and Chet Holmgren had 12 points and 17 rebounds for the Thunder.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Caleb Williams throws 2 TD passes as the Bears beat Drake Maye and the Patriots 30-24
articles.description: — Round 2 went to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears.
articles.headlineJa: カレブ・ウィリアムズが2本のTDパスを決め、ベアーズがドレイク・メイエ率いるペトリオッツに30-24で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 第2ラウンドはカレブ・ウィリアムズとシカゴ・ベアーズの勝利となった。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Round 2 went to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears.


              Williams passed for 308 yards and two touchdowns, and the Bears cooled off Drake Maye and the New England Patriots with a 30-24 victory Thursday night.


              It was the second meeting between the young quarterbacks since they were part of the 2024 NFL draft. Maye, who was selected by New England at No. 3, directed the Patriots to a 19-3 victory over Williams and the Bears when the longtime friends were rookies.


              But Williams, the No. 1 overall pick, leaned on Luther Burden and Colston Loveland while outlasting Maye and the Patriots in the rematch. Williams connected on 22 of 33 passes in his second game back after being sidelined by a right hamstring injury.


              “These nights are awesome,” Williams said. “You play against another good team on a primetime game in a short week, these games are awesome because you get to see who you are as a team. That’s who we are. We’re a smashmouth football team, an innovative team. And when things happen and things don’t go our way and the water is rocky, we stay steady.”


              Maye was 24 for 31 for 321 yards and two touchdowns. He also had a 7-yard run for New England's first TD with 11:33 left in the first half.


              But Maye also was intercepted by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson in the end zone on a pass intended for rookie tight end Eli Raridon late in the second quarter.


              “It’s those plays, I talk about it all the time,” Maye said. “You know those plays that can swing the game, can impact the game and that was definitely one of them right there. Yeah, I wish I definitely had that one back.”


              New England (4-3) had won three consecutive games behind Maye, who threw 10 TD passes and one interception during the win streak.


              “He gave us a chance," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said. "He competed and I know he’d like to have that throw back to Eli, but I thought he really competed. Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football. He gave us a chance. ... I’m glad he’s ours.”


              Burden had four catches for 130 yards for Chicago (5-2), and Loveland had a 12-yard touchdown reception. Cairo Santos kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left, a career long and matching the franchise record, after he missed a 53-yard attempt earlier in the final quarter.


              Williams became the first Bears quarterback to throw for more than 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky had a three-game run in 2018.


              “I think he did a pretty good job throughout the night,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “I know he had a number of explosive plays. He found some of those guys at the second level that were huge for us.”

articles.headline: TE Cole Kmet exits Bears' win vs. Patriots with knee injury
articles.description: Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited Thursday night's game against the Patriots on a cart after injuring his right knee in the fourth quarter.
articles.headlineJa: TEコール・クメット、ペトリオッツ戦でのベアーズ勝利の中で膝の負傷により途中交代
articles.descriptionJa: ベアーズのタイトエンド、コール・クメットは木曜夜のペトリオッツ戦で、第4クォーターに右膝を負傷し、カートで運ばれて退場した。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Bears tight end Cole Kmet exited Chicago's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night on a cart because of an injury to his right knee.

With 5:46 to play in the fourth quarter, Kmet caught an 8-yard pass from Caleb Williams and took a hard hit while running up the Bears' sideline. The tight end collided with Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez and linebacker Robert Spillane, and immediately grabbed for his knee while on the ground.

Kmet got to his feet with the help of trainers but could not put weight on his right leg. He gave the crowd at Soldier Field a thumbs-up as he was carted back to the locker room, where he was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Coach Ben Johnson said the Bears will find out more about the severity of Kmet's injury on Friday.

"I don't think it looked very good," Johnson said.

Williams had a similar response after watching Kmet leave the game with what appeared to be a serious injury.

"It was tough," Williams said. "I don't know exactly what it is and all of that, but obviously being carted off is never good. You're at least going to miss some time. I don't have the words to describe what Cole is to me, what Cole is to this team, this organization. He's the longest-tenured Bear, I believe. And so he's been through it, and it's challenging, it's tough and I'll be with him. I'll be right there with him through every step of whatever the injury is. And Cole's been there for me every step of the way through the first year, the second year and now through this year. I could only do the same for him."

Kmet finished with three catches for 28 yards. Entering Week 7, he had logged the eighth-highest snap count on offense, and he has missed only one game over his seven-year career due to injury.

"Love that guy," tight end Colston Loveland said. "We're going to miss him, for sure. I'm praying for him."

articles.headlineJa: NBA連続得点記録：知っておきたい選手の記録
articles.descriptionJa: レブロン・ジェームズ、ケビン・デュラント、SGAらは、NBAで驚異的な連続得点記録を持つ選手たちだ。その他の注目すべき記録をチェックしよう。
articles.body:
What's more impressive: scoring 100 points in a single game or scoring 60-plus points in three straight games twice in the span of a month and a half?

Wilt Chamberlain accomplished both during a dominant stretch of the 1961-62 NBA season.

One of Chamberlain's many other NBA scoring records was broken by reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. When the Oklahoma City Thunder guard scored 20 against the Boston Celtics on March 12th, it marked his 127th consecutive game with 20-plus points, breaking Chamberlain's record of 126 games (1961-63).

SGA's streak came to an end on October 22, 2026 at 141 games. In December 2025, LeBron James' streak of consecutive games with 10-plus points ended at 1,297, after scoring eight points in a win against the Toronto Raptors.

articles.headline: Caleb Williams, Bears find just enough to hold off Pats
articles.description: The Bears never trailed, but they never seemed comfortable with the lead.
articles.headlineJa: カレブ・ウィリアムズとベアーズ、パトリオッツを辛うじて退ける
articles.descriptionJa: ベアーズは一度もリードを許さなかったが、リードしている間も決して余裕があるようには見えなかった。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- There were times Thursday night when the Chicago Bears' lead over the New England Patriots looked in serious jeopardy, but each time quarterback Caleb Williams found a way to rescue his team on a night Bears fans remembered Mike Ditka. 

The last one was a 21-yard pass to Rome Odunze on third-and-9 from the Bears' 10-yard line with 4:59 left. It extended the drive, and Cairo Santos made it pay off with the longest field goal of his career, and tied for the third longest in the history of Soldier Field, from 58 yards out to secure a 30-24 victory.

Williams put up his second straight 300-yard passing game, finishing 22-of-33 for 308 yards with two touchdowns.

Luther Burden III caught all four targets and finished with 130 receiving yards and a touchdown.

The Patriots snapped a three-game win streak.

Chicago Bears (5-2)

What to make of the QB performance: Williams became the first Bears player with consecutive 300-passing yard games since Mitchell Trubisky had three straight in 2018 from Weeks 4 to 7. He's also the first Bears QB with 300 passing yards and no interceptions in consecutive games since Brian Hoyer went four straight in 2016.

Stat to know: Burden has solidified himself as the No. 1 receiver in the Bears' offense. Every catch Burden had in the first half led to points, including his 24-yard touchdown before halftime. The self-proclaimed "problem child" caused issues for the Patriots' defense all game. He's the first player this season with multiple 25-yard receptions in the first quarter alone and put together the third 100-yard receiving game of his career. He does the most with the "runner's ball" that Williams emphasizes. He has 250 yards after the catch, the second most this season by a wide receiver. Drake London has 255.

Trend to watch: The Bears' defense has multiple sacks (two vs. Drake Maye) in all seven games this season. Three other teams have multiple sacks in the first six. It's the third-longest streak for the Bears to start a season in the last 50 seasons.

Most surprising performance: Chicago stuck with its blitz-heavy approach coming off its highest blitz rate of the season in Atlanta (56.4%), but while it worked against the Falcons, it led to two of the biggest plays of the day for the Patriots. The Bears squandered the 13-point lead they built before halftime when they rushed six on the last play of the second quarter and Maye hit Rhamondre Stevenson for a 48-yard touchdown. The other longest pass play allowed -- Eli Raridon's 30-yard touchdown -- came when Chicago rushed six. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: at Seattle Seahawks (Monday, Nov. 2, ESPN)

New England Patriots (4-3)

Maye had one hiccup on an otherwise impressive night, helping keep the Patriots in a game they never led.

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.
articles.headlineJa: ウェイン・ルーニー：ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとマン・ユナイテッドの選手たちは「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っている
articles.descriptionJa: ウェイン・ルーニーは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのチームが「赤ん坊」のように振る舞っていると猛烈に批判し、ブルーノ・フェルナンデスとリサンドロ・マルティネスに自省を促した。
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.

Fernandes followed Martínez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League.

The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martínez -- who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox -- of being selfish.

Sources: Carrick to lead Man United against Bournemouth

During an appearance on "The United Stand" podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick's future, said: "When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start.

"We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn't talk, but I'd run through a brick wall for him on the pitch.

"These players, they're selfish. They care about themselves, they don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

"If they're not getting what's right for them. They're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves.

- Ogden: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Dawson: Man United were abysmal in Como, but only Carrick who will suffer

"Bruno, he's having probably the worst run of form he's had since he's been at the club and again, it's no coincidence he's putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players... they'll find what is looking back at them is them and it's not good enough."

articles.headline: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?
articles.description: The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to much more than their manager. Who deserves the most blame, and why?
articles.headlineJa: マン・Uの混乱、責任は誰にあるのか：キャリック、選手たち……それともラトクリフ？
articles.descriptionJa: ユナイテッドに関する苦い真実は、その長期化し根深い衰退の原因は監督だけではないということだ。誰が最も責められるべきであり、その理由は何か？
articles.body:
Manchester United are in crisis -- again. One of the world's biggest football clubs is in the middle of its worst start to a season in 40 years and suffered their heaviest Champions League defeat since 1994 when losing 4-1 to Como this week, so who is to blame?

Is it the owners -- the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe -- the senior executives, the manager or the players? The bitter truth about United is that their prolonged and deep-rooted decline can be attributed to all of the above.

So why does the blame lie in all areas, and what, if anything, can be done to drag United out of its doom spiral? ESPN has assessed United's problems and why nobody at Old Trafford can escape the scrutiny for the club's cycle of failure.

- Dawson: It's dire at Man United, but only Carrick will suffer

- UCL Talking Points: What to make of Man United's mess?

- Who are Como? The vacation-destination club that just rocked Man United

The Glazers

United have been owned by the Glazer family since 2005 following the completion of a controversial leveraged buyout.

The Glazers, who also own the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, purchased United for £790 million but borrowed £600 million, using the club as security for the loan, to complete the deal. As a consequence, the previously debt-free club was instantly plunged into £600m of debt.

That debt has been a millstone for United ever since and during the 21 years of Glazer ownership, over £1 billion has gone out of the club in debt repayments, accumulated interest, refinancing costs and dividends to shareholders. Every year of Glazer ownership has seen an average of £50m go out of the club on non-football costs -- a figure that could translate into a new signing or more attractive player wages.

Under the Glazers, Old Trafford has become a decaying stadium no longer fit for purpose and the team has suffered from long-term under-investment. Although the Glazers surrendered control of football operations to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Feb 2024 -- a £1.25 billion pay-day for a 27.7% stake in the club -- the nine-year period Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement as manager in 2013 and Ratcliffe's arrival was dominated by poor managerial and executive appointments by the Glazers and a woeful player recruitment record.

Everything that is going wrong at United can be traced back to the Glazers.

Percentage of blame: 50%

Sir Jim Ratcliffe

One of Britain's richest men and a lifelong United fan born less than 10 miles from Old Trafford, Ratcliffe was billed as the club's savior when he bought a 27.7% stake in exchange for control of football operations in February 2024.

He promised to overhaul the club, saying United's data analytics department was "last century," and he made an immediate impact by hiring Man City chief operating officer Omar Berrada as CEO and recruiting director football Dan Ashworth from Newcastle. articles.headline: Erling Haaland set to return with Man City 'hungry' to continue perfect start
articles.description: Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.
articles.body:
Manchester City coach Enzo Maresca said Erling Haaland is available to return for Saturday's trip to Aston Villa, while three other players remain doubtful.

Haaland, who has scored 12 goals in nine games to start to the season, remained on the bench throughout Man City's 5-1 Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens on Tuesday.

- Maresca determined to help Foden back to his best

- Walker: 'No intention' of removing Man City tattoos

- Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale

But Maresca confirmed Thursday that the Norway striker is in line to return, while Matheus Nunes, Nico O'Reilly and Mateo Kovacic had been improving as City prepare to visit Villa Park after three consecutive home games.

"We have a session this afternoon. [The injured players] can all be available or not in terms of still doubt," Maresca told a news conference. "Yesterday, they were all improving, and we'll see this afternoon. For sure, Erling is the only one 100% available."

City go into the game three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the Premier League, with Maresca having begun his first season in charge with seven straight league wins.

Despite the perfect start, the former Chelsea coach insisted the team is not resting on its laurels.

"The mood is very good," Maresca said. "I said many times the mood is good. We are happy with our start but we are more hungry for more wins. We're happy at the moment but want more.

"It's too early [to say teams are not in the title race]. Seven games, there are many games to go. It's too early."

As well as Haaland, Rayan Cherki has been another major contributor to the positive early weeks of Maresca's tenure. The France international has six goals and two assists thus far and Maresca praised Cherki as one of Europe's best players when deployed in the right areas.

"If we are able to keep him there, and if we are able to find him between the lines, so in the right position, I think he is one of the best player in Europe," Maresca said.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: In-the-dark Kane trying not to 'stress' over Monday's Ballon d'Or reveal
articles.description: Bayern striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane said he would prefer to know ahead of time whether he has won the Ballon D'Or, adding he is still in the dark over Monday's decision.

The 33-year-old is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the coveted prize since Michael Owen in 2001, but he faces competition from Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami CF's Lionel Messi among others on the 30-man shortlist.

As of 2024, organisers France Football insist they do not warn the winners in advance. That did not stop Real Madrid boycotting the event that year upon learning via a leak that Vinícius Júnior had been overlooked in favour of Rodri.

Kane scored for the tenth consecutive Champions League game on Wednesday as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Arsenal at Allianz Arena. Only Cristiano Ronaldo (11) has a longer streak in the competition's history and speaking to reporters after the game, Kane said: "They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don't know, so I can understand why.

"I think my wife would prefer to know and my family, it's very stressful for everyone. From my point of view, of course, I'd love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can't control that. We'll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

"I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rum ours flying around and you try to stay away from it. We have important games today and I know we have another important one on Sunday before the event on Monday so that's where my focus is.

"Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see."

Bayern have drawn two and won once in the League Phase of the UCL so far, leaving them in 14th place in the table. The Bundesliga champions face third-place Freiburg on Sunday as they try to remain atop of Germany's top flight.
